gallery.title: Component gallery
gallery.lead: Every component of the interface in every state, with fixture data from an invented research field. Switch the theme and the language to see them all.
gallery.section.tokens.lead: Colours, type and spacing. Black and greys on white, or the reverse; one accent for the active item and links.
gallery.section.button.lead: One primary action per view. A loading button keeps its place and its focus.
gallery.section.card.lead: A titled region, with actions and a footer when needed.
gallery.section.status.lead: The six states of a stage, told by shape: they read in black and white.
gallery.section.tracker.lead: The build’s stages with their state, why they need an update, and their progress.
gallery.section.stepper.lead: Where you are in a flow of several steps.
gallery.section.tabs.lead: Arrow keys move between tabs; the list is one tab stop.
gallery.section.table.lead: A hundred thousand rows, sortable, with keyboard navigation, range selection and a context menu. Updates keep the scroll, the focus and the selection.
gallery.section.menu.lead: Menu buttons and context menus, fully usable from the keyboard.
gallery.section.dialog.lead: The focus stays inside, Escape closes, and the focus goes back where it was.
gallery.section.toast.lead: Short messages read out by screen readers. Errors stay until dismissed.
gallery.section.form.lead: A label, a help text, the control and an error told in words.
gallery.section.empty.lead: What an empty list means, and the next thing to do.
gallery.section.error.lead: Plain words, what to do, the technical details folded away and a diagnostic to copy.
gallery.section.progress.lead: It never goes back: a lower value is ignored.
gallery.section.tooltip.lead: A hint on hover and focus; a help button for longer explanations.
gallery.section.handoff.lead: Export terms for an AI assistant, then import its answer.
gallery.section.activity.lead: The header indicator and the drawer listing jobs.
gallery.section.icons.lead: Line icons drawn in the text colour.
gallery.long.button: Rebuild every stage that needs an update, keeping the pinned map version
gallery.long.title: A card whose title is long enough to wrap onto a second line in a narrow column
gallery.long.text: A long paragraph shows how text wraps inside a component: lines stay at a comfortable length, words that are too long break rather than overflow, and the spacing around the text keeps its rhythm.
gallery.long.label: A field label long enough to need a second line on a narrow screen

themes.status.proposal: The grouping's proposal, not saved yet
themes.none.title: No themes yet
themes.none.text: Build the keywords and group them: the grouping proposes a first tree of themes, which you edit here.
themes.source.draft: This tree is the grouping's proposal. Edit it as you like: it becomes your tree when you save it.
themes.vocabulary.text: This tree is based on an earlier vocabulary: {missing, plural, one {# keyword is new} other {# keywords are new}}, {extra, plural, one {# is gone} other {# are gone}}. Rebase it: the kept keywords stay where they are, the new ones get a proposed place, marked “to check”.
themes.clean.first: Save or discard your changes first.
themes.proposal.text: The grouping ran again with other settings, on the same keywords. See its proposal as a comparison with your tree, then adopt it or keep your tree.
themes.proposal.title: A new proposal of the grouping
themes.proposal.lead: What would change if you adopted it, from your tree to the proposal. Your choice is saved as a new version, and can be undone from the versions.
themes.proposal.adopted: The proposal is now your tree
themes.proposal.kept: Your tree is kept; this proposal will not be offered again
themes.proposal.failed: The proposal could not be read
themes.check.banner: {count, plural, one {# keyword waits} other {# keywords wait}} in the “To check” queue: new keywords placed by the rebase.
themes.check.label: Keywords to check
themes.check.keys: A: accept here · M: move to… · S: set aside… · J and K: next and previous
themes.check.empty.text: When a rebase adds keywords, each waits here with its proposed place until you accept it, move it or set it aside.
themes.restored.text: Your unsaved changes of {when} were restored ({count, plural, one {# change} other {# changes}}). They are kept in this browser until you save them.
themes.restored.stale: You have unsaved changes of {when} ({count, plural, one {# change} other {# changes}}), made on an earlier version of the tree. Reload and merge: they are applied again to the current tree, and those that no longer apply are listed.
themes.stale.title: The tree was saved elsewhere
themes.stale.text: Someone saved another version of the tree since you opened it. Reload and merge: your {count, plural, one {change is} other {# changes are}} applied again to the newer tree, and nothing is saved until you save.
themes.merge.entry: {count, plural, one {Reload and merge # change} other {Reload and merge # changes}}
themes.merge.done: {count, plural, =0 {The tree was reloaded} one {Reloaded: your change applies to the newer tree} other {Reloaded: your # changes apply to the newer tree}}
themes.merge.failed: The tree could not be reloaded
themes.merge.report.title: Some changes could not be applied again
themes.merge.report.lead: {applied} of {total} changes apply to the newer tree. These no longer do:
themes.merge.report.all: Every change applies to the newer tree.
themes.discard.title: Discard your changes?
themes.discard.text: {count, plural, one {Your unsaved change is lost.} other {Your # unsaved changes are lost.}} The saved tree stays as it is.
themes.leave.title: Leave the theme editor?
themes.leave.text: {count, plural, one {Your change is not saved.} other {Your # changes are not saved.}} They stay in this browser as a draft, restored when you come back, but nobody else sees them before you save.
themes.viewing.text: You are reading the version of {when}. It is read only.
themes.preview.text: Preview of {count, plural, one {# proposed change} other {# proposed changes}} on your tree{refused, plural, =0 {} one {; # cannot be applied} other {; # cannot be applied}}. Nothing is changed until you apply them.

themes.apply.done: The themes are applied: the map shows them
themes.save.same: Nothing changed since the saved version
themes.save.removed: {count, plural, one {The empty node {names} was removed.} other {# empty nodes were removed: {names}.}}
themes.save.failed: The tree could not be saved
themes.refused.title: This change was refused

themes.search.total: {keywords, plural, one {# keyword} other {# keywords}} on {nodes, plural, one {# node} other {# nodes}}
themes.search.none: Nothing matches. Try fewer letters, or a word of another language.
themes.search.aside: {count, plural, one {# set aside} other {# set aside}}
themes.aside.empty.text: Keywords you set aside wait here, with their reason, until you put them back.
themes.aside.title: {count, plural, one {Set aside “{term}”} other {Set aside # keywords}}
themes.aside.lead: A keyword set aside stays in the project but on no theme. It keeps its reason and can be put back at any time.
themes.aside.reason.field: not a subject of this field
themes.aside.submit: {count, plural, one {Set it aside} other {Set them aside}}
themes.attr.title: {count, plural, one {What “{term}” counts toward} other {What # keywords count toward}}
themes.attr.lead: A keyword's use counts toward its node and every node above it. A broad keyword can stay where it is shown and count toward the upper levels only, or nowhere.
themes.attr.default: Its own node and the nodes above it
themes.attr.level.help: It counts toward its nodes down to “{level}”, not below.
themes.attr.none.help: Shown on its node, but its use counts toward no theme.
themes.rename.title: Rename “{name}”
themes.rename.lead: A {level}. Give it a name a researcher of the field would recognise.
themes.level.rename.title: Rename the level “{name}” ({level})
themes.level.rename.lead: The name of every node on this level, in the outline, the treemap and the map.
themes.level.insert.title: Insert a level
themes.level.insert.lead: Every keyword keeps its place; the new level repeats the level above it (or groups everything, at the top). You then split, merge and rename.
themes.level.insert.top: Above “{name}”: one new node groups everything
themes.level.insert.bottom: Below “{name}”: an empty level for finer topics
themes.level.insert.top.help: A new top level with one node that holds every current top-level node.
themes.level.insert.between.help: Each node above with nodes under it gets one new node, named like it, that takes them over.
themes.level.insert.bottom.help: No node is added: you create the finer topics and move keywords to them.
themes.level.insert.full: The tree has four levels already, the most it can have.
themes.level.remove.title: Remove a level
themes.level.remove.lead: Each node of the level dissolves into its parent, which takes over its keywords and nodes. The previous version keeps their names.
themes.level.remove.help: Their keywords and nodes go to the level above.
themes.level.remove.top.help: The top level has no parent: the keywords of its nodes are set aside, with the reason.
themes.level.remove.last: The tree has one level: it cannot lose it.
themes.move.title: {count, plural, one {Move “{term}” to…} other {Move # keywords to…}}
themes.move.lead: Choose the node, on any level. A keyword on a higher node is broader than every node below it.
themes.movenode.title: Move “{name}” under…
themes.movenode.lead: Choose its new parent: a node of the level “{level}”. Everything under it moves with it.
themes.putback.title: {count, plural, one {Put “{term}” back into…} other {Put # keywords back into…}}
themes.putback.lead: Choose the node it goes back to.
themes.merge_node.title: Merge “{name}” with…
themes.merge_node.lead: Choose the node that takes over what “{name}” holds; “{name}” then disappears. Only nodes of the same level can merge.
themes.split.title: Split “{name}”
themes.split.lead: Tick what goes to a new node beside it, and name the new node. What you do not tick stays.
themes.split.none: Tick at least one keyword or node.
themes.split.all: Leave at least one keyword or node where it is.
themes.create.lead: An empty {level}: move keywords to it next. Saving removes it if it stays empty.
themes.treemap.label: Treemap of the themes
themes.treemap.keys: Arrows: choose · Enter: zoom in · Escape: zoom out · the area is the keywords' use
themes.treemap.empty.text: Create a first node, then move keywords to it from the “Set aside” tray.
themes.map.label: Map of the people and keywords
themes.map.lead: {people, plural, one {# person} other {# people}} and {keywords, plural, one {# keyword} other {# keywords}}, coloured by theme
themes.map.keys: Drag or arrows: move · wheel or + and −: zoom · 0: fit · click: select
themes.map.status: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing highlighted} one {# point highlighted} other {# points highlighted}}
themes.map.none.text: Save and apply the themes: the build draws the map of the people and their keywords.
themes.map.note: Keywords take the colour of their theme in your tree now; the {people} people keep theirs from the last apply.

themes.panel.people_count: {count, plural, one {# person uses it} other {# people use it}}
themes.panel.no_keywords: No keyword yet: move some here.
themes.panel.people: The people who weigh most on it
themes.panel.people.none: Apply the themes to see who weighs on this node.
themes.panel.people.note: From the last apply: the share of each person's keyword use that counts toward it.
themes.panel.review.to_check: {count, plural, one {# to check} other {# to check}}
themes.panel.hint: Choose a node or a keyword in the outline, the treemap or the map: its details and actions show here. Enter moves here; the context menu key opens the actions.
themes.versions.title: Versions of the tree
themes.versions.lead: Every saved version, the current one first. A restore saves the version again as a new one: it can be undone the same way.
themes.versions.empty.text: The first save makes the first version.
themes.versions.failed: The version could not be read
themes.versions.restore_failed: The version could not be restored
themes.versions.restored: The version of {when} is the current tree again
themes.compare.version_title: The version of {when} and the current tree
themes.compare.version_lead: What changed from that version to the current tree.
themes.compare.same: The two trees hold the same themes and keywords.

themes.ai.title: AI curation of the themes
themes.ai.description: Ask an AI assistant you already use to propose changes to the tree; you review each one before anything changes.
themes.ai.lead: The tree goes to an assistant you choose, in a chat you open yourself. Nothing is sent from here.
themes.ai.contains.tree: the tree: its nodes, their names and levels
themes.ai.contains.keywords: each node's most used keywords, with how many people use each
themes.ai.contains.aside: the keywords set aside, and why

themes.ai.answer.help: Paste the whole answer, or open the answer file. Lines that are not changes are left out; the others are listed before anything changes.
